transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-11 08:00 PST / 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Myers (Redwood AE), Samira Khan (Redwood SE), Evan Lee (CSM) — Lena Ortiz (Pellion VP Eng), Marcus Ng (Pellion Head ML), Priya Desai (Pellion SRE), Tom Becker (Product)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh happy new year. We'll keep this to about 45 minutes — quick health check, run through usage/costs, a brief incident recap, and then roadmap and next steps. Samira's going to run the tech bits. Evan will pick up next steps. Sound good?

[00:23] Lena: Yep, thanks Jordan. We changed rooms so apologies if audio is off. Overall we wanted to understand cost trajectory and what we can do to avoid surprises this quarter.

[00:36] Samira: Great, I'll share some of the runbook pointers. Quick context: we saw a 3x spike in inference calls mid-November with the new feature rollout, p95 latency moved from ~120ms to ~320ms on hosted endpoints during the peak, cost increased roughly 2.6x month over month. I'm going to, uh, call out caching and batching levers.

[01:05] Marcus: Sorry to jump in — the spike was due to a marketing campaign plus a model change on our side where we increased context length. We probably should have staged the rollout better.

[01:18] Samira: Totally, that explains the KV cache cold starts — increasing context length invalidated a lot of cached prefixes. Two quick levers: 1) prefix/KV cache priming during rollout, and 2) a temporary dedicated pool for the rollout window to keep latencies bounded.

[01:45] Priya: On the incident side we saw two short degradations, both auto-recovered. Our on-call flagged high tail latencies and we hit some tokenization errors because the client used mixed encodings.

[02:10] Jordan: Right, Evan, can you put the incident timestamps in the shared doc? We want a reproducible timeline for post-mortem.

[02:22] Evan: Yep doing that now, I'll add p95/p99 and a note about the encoding mismatch.

[02:35] Tom: A few questions from product: what's the difference between spinning dedicated capacity vs staying hosted with Redwood for this? Cost and time to scale mostly.

[02:50] Samira: Short answer: Hosted gives you immediate elasticity but unit cost tends to be higher at scale; Dedicated (reserved) gives predictable throughput and lower unit cost, plus isolation. For rollout windows, you can also use burst capacity. There's a tradeoff: if you need strict VPC+KMS for compliance then Private is the option but that adds ops time.

[03:20] Lena: We do have a SOC2 audit coming in Q2 and the security team wants KMS with customer-managed keys, audit logs, and SSO. Is that supported in the dedicated offering or do we need Private?

[03:38] Jordan: Dedicated supports some key management integrations via our managed KMS connector, but for customer-managed keys and full VPC-control we recommend Redwood Private — that gives you the private control plane and HSM/KMS integration. We can map specific controls against the SOC 2 checklist.

[04:05] Marcus: How fast is a Private deployment? We don't want months-long projects.

[04:12] Samira: Average Private onboarding is 4-8 weeks depending on network approvals and firewall rules. Some customers go with Dedicated for immediate needs and then migrate to Private for compliance deadlines.

[04:38] Priya: For the immediate quarter we need to lock down costs. What are the low-lift optimizations?

[04:45] Samira: Quick wins: quantization profiles (we have pre-tested 4-bit profiles for some open models), request-side batching where you control grouping keys, and prefix caching. Also model selection — moving to a slightly smaller variant for high-volume non-critical traffic. We'll send a recommendation matrix.

[05:12] Jordan: On pricing — Jordan: we'll send a pilot package: 3-week dedicated pool with commit tiers and an estimated cost model. We had discussed a pilot discount on reserved commits.

[05:30] Lena: That would help. Also we need transparency on per-route token costs — the console needs to show per-model/per-route breakdown.

[05:42] Evan: The Console already has token-level breakdowns and route filters, we'll confirm retention windows and create a quick tour for your finance team.

[06:00] Marcus: Can we run a benchmark that mirrors our traffic profile? Long tail user prompts, lots of short transactional calls, and some long context sessions.

[06:12] Samira: Yes — Samira: we'll share a benchmark template. Important: please provide a representative 24–72 hour trace with anonymized data. We'll run p50/p95/p99 and cost per 1M tokens estimates across hosted/dedicated/quantized variants.

[06:35] Tom: If we send traces, what's the SLA on results?

[06:40] Samira: Typical turnaround is 5 business days for a first pass. If you want custom kernel tuning or on-prem kernel compilation that takes longer.

[07:00] Lena: Security caveat: our legal team requires, uh, that logs are retained for 12 months and that audit exports are available for auditors. How does Redwood handle that?

[07:12] Jordan: We have audit log exports at multiple retention tiers; for Private you can set retention, and for Dedicated we can push a compliance package. We'll share SOC 2 artifact links and our data flow diagram.

[07:35] Priya: One more SRE-specific ask: can you quantify cold-start time for models with large KV caches after a restart? We saw a 30–40 second tail for some nodes during the November event.

[07:48] Samira: That sounds like a KV-cache rehydration issue. For large contexts the runtime does a streaming fill which can show a spike. Options: warm-warm pools, checkpointed caches, and client-side graceful degradation with a shorter context fallback. We'll detail the runbook.

[08:15] Marcus: Are there any competitors that do this better out of the box? We evaluated Anthropic's hosted offering for one feature.

[08:22] Jordan: Competitors may have simpler setup but fewer production levers for batching/caching and fewer observability primitives — Redwood's differentiation is the combo of serving runtime + rollout tooling. But we'll be transparent about tradeoffs.

[08:45] Tom: Can we get a cost model showing the tipping point where Dedicated becomes cheaper?

[08:50] Evan: Yep — Evan: Jordan and I will run a usage curve and show break-even points; we'll include quantization scenarios.

[09:05] Lena: Ok, timeline and commitments: Security needs SOC 2 artifacts by Jan 25, Product wants pilot pricing by Jan 13, and ML wants the benchmark run by Jan 21. Can we align?

[09:20] Jordan: Yes — Jordan: Jan 13 pricing, Jan 14 benchmark template, Jan 15 sample traffic upload, Jan 21 benchmark results. If those stretch we'll adjust but that's the target.

[09:35] Priya: One last operational question: how does rollback work if a model variant causes regressions in quality? We need canary and auto-fallback.

[09:45] Samira: We support canary rollouts (percent-based), A/B, and automatic fallback to a pinned variant on error thresholds. You can define route-level fallback policies in the Console. We'll include an example policy.

[10:05] Tom: Alright that's helpful. Anything else?

[10:10] Marcus: Just one request: for the benchmark, can you include a cost per feature estimate — like per-search vs per-summarize?

[10:18] Samira: We'll map requests to tags and provide per-route cost.

[10:28] Evan: To recap next steps — Jordan will send pilot pricing and SOC 2 artifacts, Samira will send benchmark template and runbook, Pellion to upload sample traffic, Evan will schedule the follow-up. We'll target a SE deep dive week of Jan 18.

[10:45] Lena: Great, thanks everyone.

[10:50] Jordan: Thanks — we'll follow up in email and update the CRM. End call.

Note: Transcript contains some auto-caption noise: "K-V cash" appears where KV cache was meant, "S-O-C two" instead of SOC 2 in places, and occasional speaker label swaps.
